text_note.zh: 原始资料第七句作“暗凝伫”。通行本（如《宋词三百首》）多作“黯凝伫”，“黯”是心情黯然、伤感的意思，这里从通行本。两个字读音相同。
text_note.en: The source text writes line 7 with a character meaning "dark, secretly". Common editions such as Three Hundred Song Lyrics use a character meaning "gloomy, downcast", used here. Both are read àn.

readings.zh: 燕台：这里的“燕”是地名、诗题用字，读 yān，不读燕子的 yàn。
readings.en: yān tái: here the character is part of a place name and poem title, read yān, not yàn as in "swallow".

readings.zh: 重到：再一次来到，“重”读 chóng。
readings.en: chóng dào: coming again. Here the character means "again" and is read chóng.

glosses.zh: 章台路：章台本是汉代长安的一条街，后来常指歌女们住的街巷。这里指词人旧日常去的地方。
glosses.en: zhāng tái lù: Zhangtai was a street in Han-dynasty Chang'an. Later the name stood for the lanes where singing girls lived. Here it is the place the poet often visited long ago.

glosses.zh: 还见：又看到。
glosses.en: hái jiàn: again I see.

glosses.zh: 褪粉梅梢：梅花已经开过，颜色褪去了。
glosses.en: tuì fěn méi shāo: plum branches whose blossoms have faded.

glosses.zh: 试花：刚开始开花。
glosses.en: shì huā: just beginning to blossom.

glosses.zh: 愔愔：安安静静的样子。
glosses.en: yīn yīn: quiet and still.

glosses.zh: 坊陌：街巷。
glosses.en: fāng mò: streets and lanes.

glosses.zh: 定巢：安顿好窝，住下来。
glosses.en: dìng cháo: settling into a nest.

glosses.zh: 黯凝伫：心情低落，久久地站着出神。
glosses.en: àn níng zhù: downcast, standing still for a long time, lost in thought.

glosses.zh: 个人：那个人，指他从前喜欢的女子。
glosses.en: gè rén: that person, the girl he once loved.

glosses.zh: 痴小：年纪小，天真不懂事。
glosses.en: chī xiǎo: young and innocent.

glosses.zh: 乍窥门户：刚开始在门口探头张望，还是个小姑娘。
glosses.en: zhà kuī mén hù: just starting to peek out of the doorway, still a young girl.

glosses.zh: 侵晨：天快亮的时候，清早。
glosses.en: qīn chén: at early dawn.

glosses.zh: 浅约宫黄：淡淡地在额头涂上黄色的妆。宫黄是古代女子画在额头上的黄粉。
glosses.en: qiǎn yuē gōng huáng: lightly dabbing yellow makeup on her brow. "Palace yellow" was a yellow powder women painted on the forehead.

glosses.zh: 障风映袖：抬起袖子挡风，脸映在袖子边。
glosses.en: zhàng fēng yìng xiù: raising her sleeve against the wind, her face framed by it.

glosses.zh: 盈盈：姿态美好的样子。
glosses.en: yíng yíng: graceful and lovely.

glosses.zh: 前度刘郎：上一次来过的刘郎。唐代诗人刘禹锡有诗句“前度刘郎今又来”，这里词人用来比自己旧地重游。
glosses.en: qián dù liú láng: Master Liu who came before. The Tang poet Liu Yuxi wrote of himself as "Master Liu who came before, now here again". The poet borrows the phrase for his own return.

glosses.zh: 访邻寻里：到街坊邻居家去打听。
glosses.en: fǎng lín xún lǐ: asking around among the neighbors.

glosses.zh: 同时歌舞：当年一起唱歌跳舞的人。
glosses.en: tóng shí gē wǔ: the girls who sang and danced at the same time as her.

glosses.zh: 秋娘：唐代有名的歌女常叫秋娘，后来泛指歌女。
glosses.en: qiū niáng: a name often used by famous Tang singing girls, later used for any singer.

glosses.zh: 声价如故：名气还和从前一样。
glosses.en: shēng jià rú gù: as famous as ever.

glosses.zh: 吟笺赋笔：在纸上写诗作词。
glosses.en: yín jiān fù bǐ: writing poems on paper.

glosses.zh: 燕台句：唐代李商隐写过《燕台》诗。洛阳一个叫柳枝的姑娘听人念了这些诗，很喜欢，便打听作者。这里比喻那个女子曾经喜爱词人的作品。
glosses.en: yān tái jù: the Tang poet Li Shangyin wrote poems called "Yantai". A Luoyang girl named Liuzhi heard someone recite them, loved them, and asked who the poet was. Here it means the girl once loved the poet's own verses.

glosses.zh: 知谁伴：不知道现在谁陪着她。
glosses.en: zhī shuí bàn: who knows who is with her now.

glosses.zh: 露饮：在露天里饮酒。
glosses.en: lù yǐn: drinking in the open air.

glosses.zh: 闲步：悠闲地散步。
glosses.en: xián bù: strolling at leisure.

glosses.zh: 孤鸿：一只孤单的大雁。
glosses.en: gū hóng: a lone wild goose.

glosses.zh: 探春：出门游春，寻找春天的景色。
glosses.en: tàn chūn: going out to look for spring.

glosses.zh: 意绪：心情。
glosses.en: yì xù: feelings, mood.

glosses.zh: 官柳：官府在大路两边种的柳树。
glosses.en: guān liǔ: willows planted by the government along the main roads.

glosses.zh: 金缕：金色的丝线，比喻嫩黄的柳条。
glosses.en: jīn lǚ: golden threads, meaning the new yellow-green willow twigs.

glosses.zh: 归骑：骑马回去。
glosses.en: guī qí: riding home.

glosses.zh: 纤纤：细细的。
glosses.en: xiān xiān: fine and thin.

glosses.zh: 断肠：伤心到极点。
glosses.en: duàn cháng: heartbroken.

glosses.zh: 风絮：随风飘飞的柳絮。
glosses.en: fēng xù: willow fluff blowing in the wind.

translation.zh: 又走上了章台路，
translation.en: I walk Zhangtai Road again.

translation.zh: 又看到梅花开过、颜色褪去的枝梢，
translation.en: Again I see plum branches whose blossoms have faded,

translation.zh: 和刚刚开花的桃树。
translation.en: and peach trees just coming into bloom.

translation.zh: 街巷里的人家安安静静，
translation.en: The houses along the lanes are quiet.

translation.zh: 找好窝的燕子，
translation.en: The swallows that have found their nests

translation.zh: 又飞回了旧日的地方。
translation.en: have flown back to their old homes.

translation.zh: 我心情低落，久久地站着出神。
translation.en: Downcast, I stand still a long while, lost in thought.

translation.zh: 想起那个人当年还小，天真烂漫，
translation.en: I remember her when she was young and innocent,

translation.zh: 刚开始在门口探头张望。
translation.en: just beginning to peek out of the doorway.

translation.zh: 清早，她在额上淡淡地涂了黄妆，
translation.en: At dawn she dabbed a little yellow on her brow,

translation.zh: 抬起袖子挡风，
translation.en: raised her sleeve against the wind,

translation.zh: 说说笑笑，模样那么可爱。
translation.en: and laughed and chatted so sweetly.

translation.zh: 如今，我像当年的刘郎一样又来了，
translation.en: Now, like Master Liu of old, I have come back.

translation.zh: 向街坊邻居打听，
translation.en: I ask among the neighbors

translation.zh: 当年和她一起唱歌跳舞的人。
translation.en: about those who sang and danced with her back then.

translation.zh: 只有旧日那位秋娘，
translation.en: Only the old singer Qiuniang

translation.zh: 名气还和从前一样。
translation.en: is still as famous as before.

translation.zh: 当年我提笔写诗作词，
translation.en: Back then I wrote poems for her,

translation.zh: 还记得她喜爱我诗句的情景。
translation.en: and I still remember how she loved my lines.

translation.zh: 不知道现在谁陪着她，
translation.en: Who keeps her company now,

translation.zh: 在名园里露天饮酒，
translation.en: drinking in the open in famous gardens,

translation.zh: 在东城悠闲散步？
translation.en: strolling at leisure in the east of town?

translation.zh: 往事都像孤雁一样飞走了。
translation.en: The past has flown off like a lone wild goose.

translation.zh: 这次出来游春，
translation.en: This spring outing

translation.zh: 满心都是离别的伤感。
translation.en: is filled with the sorrow of parting.

translation.zh: 路边的柳树垂下金线一样的嫩枝。
translation.en: Roadside willows hang low their golden threads.

translation.zh: 我骑马回去，天已经晚了，
translation.en: I ride home late,

translation.zh: 细细的雨点飘落在池塘上。
translation.en: as fine rain drifts over the pond.

translation.zh: 那叫人伤心的院子里，
translation.en: In the courtyard that breaks my heart,

translation.zh: 满帘都是随风飘飞的柳絮。
translation.en: the curtain is filled with willow fluff blowing in the wind.

background.zh: 这首词写的是词人多年以后旧地重游、寻访旧日恋人而找不到的故事。一说是周邦彦离开京城汴京（今河南开封）到外地做官多年，后来回到京城时写的，具体时间说法不一。词分三段：第一段写眼前春景依旧；第二段回忆那个女子年少的样子；第三段写人去楼空，只剩伤感。
background.en: This lyric tells of the poet returning to an old place years later, looking for a girl he once loved, and not finding her. One view says Zhou Bangyan wrote it when he came back to the capital, Bianjing (today's Kaifeng in Henan), after many years as an official elsewhere. Views on the exact date differ. It has three parts. The first shows the spring scene, unchanged. The second recalls the girl in her youth. The third finds her gone and leaves only sorrow.

author_note.zh: 周邦彦（1056—1121），字美成，号清真居士，北宋词人。他精通音乐，作品结构讲究，常常把眼前的景、过去的事和此刻的心情来回穿插。这首《瑞龙吟》就是这样：从今天写到过去，又从过去回到今天，是他最有名的作品之一。
author_note.en: Zhou Bangyan (1056–1121), courtesy name Meicheng, was a Northern Song lyric poet. He was an expert in music, and his works are carefully built. He often moves back and forth between the scene in front of him, the past, and his feelings now. This lyric does exactly that: from today to the past, then back to today. It is one of his most famous works.

appreciation.zh: 这首词像一次“回到老地方”的散步。第一段，景色一点没变：梅花谢了，桃花开了，燕子也回到老窝。燕子能回旧处，人呢？第二段，词人站在那里出神，想起那个女孩小时候的样子：清早化着淡妆，用袖子挡风，说说笑笑。写得很细，好像就在眼前。第三段回到现实：他到处打听，只有旧日的歌女还在，她却不见了。他还记得当年为她写诗的日子，可往事已经像孤雁飞走。最后，柳条低垂，细雨飘在池塘上，满帘柳絮乱飞，这些景物把说不出的伤心都装了进去。
appreciation.en: This lyric is like a walk back to an old place. In the first part nothing has changed: the plum blossoms are gone, the peach trees are blooming, and the swallows are back in their old nests. The swallows can come home, but what about people? In the second part the poet stands lost in thought and remembers the girl when she was young: light makeup at dawn, a sleeve raised against the wind, laughing and chatting. The details are so fine she seems to be right there. The third part returns to the present. He asks everywhere. Only an old singer is still around, and the girl is gone. He still remembers writing poems for her, but the past has flown off like a lone goose. At the end, willows hang low, fine rain falls on the pond, and willow fluff fills the curtain. These scenes hold all the sadness he cannot put into words.
